# Task Spec Template

> This document defines the canonical template for task spec files generated by DevLoop.  
> Coding agents MUST read this before generating task specs.

---

## Authoring Rules

> 16 rules split into two blocks: **(A) Spec quality** — what must be documented before implementation starts; **(B) Implementation quality** — frequent mistakes to prevent during coding.
> Each rule uses operational language (MUST / NEVER / ALWAYS) with ❌/✅ examples.
> Guidance: Adapt to project conventions. Replace class names and patterns with the project's actual domain terms.

---

### Block A — Spec Quality Rules (R-1 to R-8)

These rules govern what must be present in the task spec **before any implementation begins**.

- **R-1:** Every task spec MUST include a `## Decision Tree` section with ALL business branches covered.

  ❌ Decision tree omitted or partially described in prose  
  ✅ Explicit `GIVEN / IF / THEN` tree covering all success paths, error paths, and edge cases

- **R-2:** Every branch in the decision tree MUST have a corresponding acceptance scenario.

  ❌ Decision tree has 4 branches but only 2 scenarios are written  
  ✅ One `Scenario:` block per branch, each with a unique `Given / When / Then`

- **R-3:** Acceptance scenarios MUST be deterministic (given → when → then, no ambiguity).

  ❌ `Then the system handles it correctly`  
  ✅ `Then the response resultType is "REJECTED" and errorCode is "ERR_EXPIRED"`

- **R-4:** Data models referenced in task specs MUST reference the complete structure from `data-model.md`, not inline partial definitions.

  ❌ `Input: { id, name }` inline in the spec  
  ✅ `Input: see \`RequestFormDto\` in \`data-model.md § RequestFormDto\``

- **R-5:** Every framework API call in a task spec MUST be validated against `framework-api-registry.md` before inclusion.

  ❌ Spec calls `repo.findByIdOrFail(id)` without verifying the method exists  
  ✅ Method confirmed in `framework-api-registry.md § Repository API` before writing the spec

- **R-6:** All required features MUST be listed explicitly; no implicit "also do X" allowed.

  ❌ `Implement the save flow (and validation as usual)`  
  ✅ Separate line items for: save, field validation, error registration, response mapping

- **R-7:** Forms/DTOs consumed and produced MUST be declared with their full field structure reference.

  ❌ `Returns a success response`  
  ✅ `Returns \`ApiSuccessResponseDto\` — see \`data-model.md § ApiSuccessResponseDto\``

- **R-8:** Error keys MUST be mapped to domain constants before coding begins; no inline string literals for error codes.

  ❌ `Throw exception with code "INVALID_STATE"`  
  ✅ `Throw \`AppException(Constants.Errors.INVALID_STATE)\``

---

### Block B — Implementation Quality Rules (R-9 to R-16)

These rules prevent the most frequent implementation mistakes. Violations are **build blockers**.

> Guidance: Examples below are illustrative. Replace class names, annotations, and syntax with the project's actual stack as defined in `guardrails.md` and `anti-patterns.md`.

- **R-9:** NEVER use Partial Form Models — request/response objects MUST carry the complete field set declared in the spec (AP-3).

  ❌ A request object passed to a service carrying only 3 of the 7 fields declared in the spec; remaining fields are silently ignored  
  ✅ The request object contains all fields declared in `data-model.md` for that operation

- **R-10:** Request/response objects at the API boundary MUST follow the project's naming convention for API-layer types, as defined in `guardrails.md` (AP-6).

  ❌ An internal domain object used directly as the HTTP request/response payload  
  ✅ A dedicated API-layer object named according to the project's convention (e.g., prefixed, suffixed, or in a dedicated package)

- **R-11:** NEVER create an interface paired with a single implementation when no polymorphism is needed (AP-7).

  ❌ `TaskService` interface + `TaskServiceImpl` class — only one implementation exists and none is planned  
  ✅ A single concrete `TaskService` class registered as a component

- **R-12:** Unit tests MUST NOT load the full application context — use the project's approved isolated unit testing approach instead.

  ❌ A unit test that starts the full application context to test a single service method  
  ✅ A lightweight unit test that injects mocks directly into the class under test, with no framework bootstrap

- **R-13:** ALWAYS guard collection or array access before use; NEVER assume a collection or its elements are non-null.

  ❌ Directly accessing `list[0]` or chaining `.get(0)` without a prior null/empty check  
  ✅ Check that the collection is non-null and non-empty before accessing any element

- **R-14:** ALWAYS guard map key lookups before dereferencing the result; NEVER assume a key is present.

  ❌ `map.get("key").value` — crashes if the key is absent  
  ✅ Retrieve the value, check for null/absence, then use it

- **R-15:** NEVER call system time directly in service code — inject a time provider abstraction so tests can control the clock.

  ❌ `now = getCurrentDate()` or equivalent built-in called directly inside a service method  
  ✅ A clock or time-provider dependency injected into the service constructor; tests pass a fixed instant

- **R-16:** NEVER put business logic in the entry-point layer (controller, handler, route) — it MUST only extract input and delegate to the service layer.

  ❌ A controller that evaluates business conditions, queries a repository, or catches domain exceptions directly  
  ✅ The controller extracts the request parameters, calls `service.execute(...)`, and maps the result to a response object

## Decision Tree

> To be populated per feature task spec.  
> Template structure:

Guidance: Replace `<entity-id>` and response/action types with the project's actual domain terms.

```
GIVEN <entity-id>
  ├─ IF [condition A]
  │    → THEN [action / return <SuccessResponse> with resultType = X]
  ├─ IF [condition B]
  │    → THEN [action / return <SuccessResponse> with resultType = Y]
  └─ IF [unexpected error]
       → THEN catch → [error-registration call] → rethrow <DomainException>
```

---

## Acceptance Scenario Template

Guidance: Replace placeholders with the domain terms used in the project (entity IDs, state names, response fields).

```gherkin
Scenario: [Short description]
  Given [entity] with id "<entity-id>"
  And [relevant precondition / data state]
  When the task "<task-name>" is executed
  Then the response is "<expected-result-type>"
  And [state is updated with ...]
  And [no errors are recorded] OR [errors are recorded as ...]
```

---

## Standard Task Spec Sections

Guidance: Keep all sections. Remove or rename items in parentheses to match project conventions.

1. **Overview** — intent, owning service, framework dependencies
2. **Input** — primary entity ID (always), additional parameters or injected references
3. **External Dependencies** — which external services or APIs are called
4. **Decision Tree** — all business branches (mandatory)
5. **Data Changes** — which data models or forms are read and/or written
6. **Error Handling** — error codes and their mapping to domain constants
7. **Acceptance Scenarios** — one per decision tree branch
8. **Implementation Notes** — non-obvious technical decisions

---

## §9 Test Specification

> To be filled for every task. All subsections are mandatory unless explicitly marked optional.
> Guidance: This section defines the structural contract for test coverage. The concrete conventions (test framework, mock library, fixture location, profile mechanism) are defined in `testing-strategy.md` and `guardrails.md` — always read those documents and adapt accordingly.

### 9.1 Fixtures Layer

> Create reusable test fixtures before writing any test. One fixture builder per entity or data object.

- Fixtures MUST be placed in the project's designated test fixtures location (see `testing-strategy.md`)
- Fixtures MUST be shared across unit and integration tests — never duplicated
- Each fixture MUST provide at least a `valid()` factory and targeted variants for specific states (e.g., `withState(...)`, `expired()`, `withError(...)`)

### 9.2 Unit Tests

**Structure requirements:**

- Use the project's approved isolated unit testing approach (framework and mock library defined in `testing-strategy.md`)
- Do NOT load the full application context in unit tests
- Do NOT mock static utility helpers that have no injectable counterpart — call them directly
- Inject configuration values via the project's approved test setup mechanism

**Error branch mandatory verifications — all of the following are required per error branch:**

1. **Exception is thrown** — assert that the method under test raises an exception of the expected type
2. **Error was registered** — verify that the error-reporting collaborator was called with the correct arguments
3. **Error code is correct** — verify the exact error code or identifier passed to the error-reporting call; do not rely solely on the fact that a call was made

> ⚠️ A test that only verifies the error-reporting call was made without asserting the exception is thrown is **incomplete** — it cannot detect swallowed exceptions. All three checks are required.

### 9.3 Integration / Slice Tests

> Guidance: Describe which integration slice applies to this task (e.g., HTTP layer, persistence layer, messaging). List the endpoints, queries, or messages under test.

- Use the project's approved integration testing slice (defined in `testing-strategy.md`)
- Mock external dependencies at the appropriate boundary
- At least one happy-path and one error-path scenario per public entry point

### 9.4 Test Helpers

List any shared helpers, custom matchers, or test utilities needed for this task. Always check the project's existing test helper location before creating new ones.

### 9.5 Coverage Thresholds

| Scope | Required coverage |
|---|---|
| Component under test | ≥ project minimum (see `testing-strategy.md`) |
| Error branches | 100% — every error path must have a dedicated test |
| Entry-point layer | ≥ 1 test per operation + corresponding error path |

### 9.6 Application Context Smoke Test (mandatory)

Every module MUST have a test that verifies the full application context loads correctly using the test configuration profile.

- The test configuration profile MUST activate the test-specific environment settings (URLs, credentials, feature flags)
- Without the test profile, external service URLs are not overridden and tests will attempt real connections
- See `guardrails.md` for the required profile activation mechanism and `testing-strategy.md` for the configuration file template
